summary: begin_turn() unconditionally discards the turn's delivery-context-recorded flag and queue() calls it for every chunk, so queuing a later chunk erases proof that earlier delivered speech was committed to conversation context.
failure_scenario: Chunk 1 of turn T is queued with an admission, played, and mark_delivered_confirmed + consume_delivery_confirmation (context.py:484) records it, so snapshot_turn_counts(T).assistant_delivery_context_recorded is True. Chunk 2 of T is then queued (streaming.py:1612 queues per sentence, once synthesis outpaces nothing, i.e. whenever chunk 2 is queued after chunk 1 was already delivered); the flag is now False. The turn snapshot/settlement (streaming.py:1739/1819 -> evidence/admission.py:3098) then reports model_context_admitted=False / assistant_delivery_context_recorded=False for a turn whose heard text is in the model context.
evidence: Isolated synthetic repro against DeliveredSpeechLedger using the public API (queue with admission, mark_started, mark_delivered_confirmed, consume_delivery_confirmation, snapshot_turn_counts): prints True before the second queue() and False after it. Passing control: with chunk 2 queued before chunk 1's confirmation is consumed the flag stays True, so the loss is timing-dependent. End-to-end frequency in production was not measured; the streaming consumer path (begin_turn at streaming.py:1215 once per turn, queue per chunk at 1612) was read statically. test_delivery.py does not cover a second queue() after consumption.

summary: A latched binding terminal error is re-raised by every close_binding(), and ReconnectSafeConversationWorker clears its binding only after a successful close, so one failed binding blocks every later bind() on that runtime.
failure_scenario: The STT push raises a RuntimeError (transient provider failure) inside receive_audio -> _latch_terminal_error. The LiveKit disconnect/reconnect path then calls runtime.close_binding() (livekit/worker.py:252,312), which raises the latched error; _binding is never cleared, so bind() (worker.py:1219) fails the same way on each retry and no new generation is ever admitted until the whole runtime is replaced. The close operation is not re-run because _ensure_binding_close only retries on timeout/needs_retry, and terminal errors set neither.
evidence: Isolated repro (scratchpad pytest importing test_worker helpers; the 91 imported tests also passed): after a failing STT push, three consecutive ReconnectSafeConversationWorker.close_binding() calls and a following bind() each raised the same RuntimeError, and active_generation stayed 1. Control: without the failing push, bind() replaces the binding and returns generation 2 (existing tests at test_worker.py:691). test_failed_barge_in_cancellation_cannot_admit_transcript asserts the repeated close raise but nothing asserts recovery. Whether the host rebuilds the whole runtime after this failure (which would make it an accepted fail-closed limit) was not traced; the claim is verified at the worker level only.

summary: Prior claim worker.py:670 (utterance discarded when the assistant turn ends naturally during barge-in confirmation): reproduced by reading. cancel_if_active returns False once the turn no longer owns foreground (streaming.py:1393), _confirm_interruption_from_transcript then sets authority_revoked, and _with_playback_authority returns () for later partials and the final, so the ticket is revoked as playback_authority_revoked. This is the deliberate fail-closed echo policy and no accepted contract was found requiring recovery; no test covers the natural-end case. Disposition: accepted tradeoff / unresolved (missing witness: a design statement on whether a non-echo-dominated, verifier-confirmed utterance may be retained once the foreground ended).

Prior claim worker.py:633 (short finals such as 'No.'/'OK.' dropped in the post-playback echo tail): by reading, when stt_streams_partials is true (host_launcher.py:2618, moonshine only) and confirmation is required, a final is admitted only after a partial with >=3 alphanumerics, so a 2-character answer is dropped and the ticket revoked as utterance_abandoned with no user-visible signal. Not executed; no doc or test states the 3-character threshold as a contract. Disposition: accepted tradeoff / unresolved, same fail-closed root as the worker.py:670 entry.
Prior claim speech/delivery.py:231: reproduced (see the delivery.py:237 finding). The line attribution there is begin_turn, not queue itself.

speech/word_boundary.py and speech/segmentation.py read in full: word_boundary_stop bounds, cap break, multi-channel indexing and fade_out gain end exactly at zero are consistent; DurationBoundedSynthesizer preserves exact text/PCM (checked by joined-equality), enforces operation cancellation, depth and attempt budgets, and _split_qualified_chunk verifies monotonicity and byte-identical reassembly. No defect found. Not executed beyond reading.

Scope limit: conversation/streaming.py (2555 lines), context.py, ingress.py, livekit/adapter.py, livekit/playback.py and livekit/worker.py were only skimmed at the call sites named above, not audited line by line; the absence of further findings there is not evidence of soundness. Dependencies were available via uv run; no full test matrix, ruff or mypy was run.
